prompt:
Create one finished editorial botanical poster for a weekend houseplant market, a single flat opaque landscape 16:9 artwork for SNS. 요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력.

Whole design: an open, actively drawn botanical atlas spread where the substantial explanatory paragraph is the FIRST verbal encounter, beside crossing living canopies, then leads down a short shared alignment into a horizontal market visit ledger carried by the specimens' gently stepped ground. The compact identity names this experience quietly beside the paragraph entry. Plants and copy must organize one complete field, rather than a text board with three small decorative specimens.

Draw independent plants at very different living scales across the entire width: a small broad-leaf houseplant with distinct petioles in a low clay pot, a spreading branching medium houseplant in a restrained blue pot, and a taller indoor tree whose richly articulated canopy enters the upper crop and whose woody trunk extends visibly to its planter. Arrange their shared ground heights in a gentle descent across the landscape. Give each leaf a convincing stem attachment, believable growth direction and fine vein anatomy; make real pot rims, visible soil, and one carefully limited root-ball cutaway with branching roots to convey attentive repotting and long-term care. The canopies overlap at uneven heights around and between the reading openings. Large living leaf masses, independent stems and the ground rhythm must have substantial presence, not equal isolated little icons. A viewer should feel the pleasure of choosing a plant at a suitable scale and understanding how it grows at home. No species names, measurement marks, labels or incidental lettering.

Medium and finish: observed colored pencil with fine ink linework, mineral greens, deep olive, warm bark brown and sparing mineral blue. Rich dark leaf masses balanced by open internal drawing and varied leaf fronts/backs. A light warm paper field is the integral atlas page, with selective pencil grain inside botanical forms and a clean text field. Keep all copy precisely planar and sharply typeset in very dark olive ink, without pencil noise through glyphs. Flat poster, no photographed paper, frame, room mockup, cast page shadow, stickers or tape requirement.

Typography and reading route: place the COMPLETE explanatory entry in a broad stable three-line opening adjoining a crossing canopy. Use a mature Korean book serif: full proportioned syllable bodies, ample open counters, moderately strong strokes including robust fine strokes, controlled triangular terminals, consistent weight and calm meaningful word spaces. It should read with the optical presence of roughly 18–20px body at an assumed 720px-wide SNS view, a design starting point, not an invented native output size. Do not shrink this explanation into a caption. Its paragraph area and dark weight lead the verbal hierarchy. Compose its three lines at the sentence boundary and then after the word meaning light-and, keeping the final sentence part as an easy third line. Soft wrapping may adjust to preserve full words and comfortable reading; no isolated syllable or punctuation.

Set the Korean title, Latin companion and slogan as one compact, clearly quieter identity group adjoining the paragraph's entry, not three competing headlines. The title is a calm book-serif name at smaller scale than the broad explanatory block; the Latin line has a compatible restrained serif form, and the supporting slogan is still legible.

Immediately below the paragraph's final line, begin the market name on the same optical starting axis. Date, hours and venue extend horizontally nearby along the actual specimens' stepped shared ground, with aligned baselines and deliberate group gaps. The market name and practical row are one connected family; use enough horizontal span and clear light ground to read the full useful strings. Access and the care offer form a next local row; invitation and URL complete the same ledger directly nearby. No separate right visit column and no return across a plant image to find the URL. Let pot/soil edges and ground rhythm relate to these baselines while leaves remain outside the glyph contours. Do not split useful strings between different specimens or place unrelated lines in distant corners. Date/hours/venue, access/care, invitation/URL all need comfortable dark contrast and visible bodies at 720 width, with stable Korean/Latin/numeral size and weight. Keep range dashes as clearly extended midline forms distinct from short hyphens; keep numeric baselines, colons, middle dots, ampersand, periods, URL characters, and all meaningful word spaces exactly.
